newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam securities exchange remains distant goal.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam securities exchange remains distant goal.

text.p: Vietnam indicated on Monday that plans for the communist country's first securities exchange faced indefinite delays while officials sought to establish the right conditions.

Le Van Chau, Chairman of the State Securities Committee, said in an interview that while government policy called for the early launch of an exchange, the overriding priority was to start with one that worked.

"The collapse of a prematurely inaugurated securities market would be a much greater disaster for the country's economy than a delayed start," he was quoted as saying by the monthly Vietnam Economic Times.
Chau said that at present Vietnam had neither sufficient trained personnel nor a viable minimum number of buyers and sellers to make an exchange work.
He added that more goods and a "decent operating environment" would be needed before plans could proceed, and it was too early therefore to set any realistic opening date.
"Basically, in Vietnam we have to create all of these elements virtually from scratch. There is a sea of difficulties and it certainly won't happen overnight," he said.
Vietnam's government, encouraged by the success of its market-oriented reforms, has been planning a securities bourse for several years.
But over the past 18 months officials have backpedalled on plans for its imminent establishment.
Primitive accounting systems, a nascent domestic banking industry, poor information channels and an absence of instruments to be traded are seen as the main obstacles.
Officials acknowledge that an exchange is unlikely to be established before the end of the decade.
